statement:
A Noetherian local ring $A$ is *Gorenstein* if $A[0]$ is a dualizing complex (equivalently its self-injective dimension is finite). A general Noetherian ring is Gorenstein when all local rings are. An object of the derived category is *invertible* if it admits a two-sided derived-tensor inverse; locally it is a shift of a rank-one projective module. A *local complete intersection* map is locally a quotient of a polynomial algebra by a Koszul-regular sequence.

Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A$ has a dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is Gorenstein $\Leftrightarrow$ $\omega_A^\bullet$ is an invertible
object of $D(A)$,
\item $A_\mathfrak p$ is Gorenstein $\Leftrightarrow$
$(\omega_A^\bullet)_\mathfrak p$ is an invertible object of
$D(A_\mathfrak p)$,
\item $\{\mathfrak p \in \Spec(A) \mid A_\mathfrak p\text{ is Gorenstein}\}$
is an open subset.
\end{enumerate}
\item If $A$ is Gorenstein, then $A$ has a dualizing complex if and
only if $A[0]$ is a dualizing complex.
\end{enumerate}

A derived-invertible object is locally a shift of an invertible module, not necessarily a module in degree zero.
